_comment: One overlay curve. {title} and {filled_label} are filled in per curve. A section tagged with curve kinds (equation, function, parametric, points) shows for those only: a function curve shows its source in a code editor, a parametric curve its x(t), y(t) and t range, a point set its t values and labels.

sections.label: {title}
sections.description: Show the curve on the plot.

sections.label: Equation: y =
sections.description: y as a function of x; every other name is a parameter.

sections.label: Where:
sections.description: Definitions evaluated first, in order, separated by ';' (omega = 2*pi*f*harmonic*1e-3; tau = tan(t)/omega); x and y may use them.

sections.label: x(t) =
sections.description: x as a function of t; every name that is not t, a definition or a maths function is a parameter.

sections.label: y(t) =
sections.description: y as a function of t.

sections.label: to
sections.description: Where the curve ends (t1); it is traced with the tab's number of points.

sections.label: t values:
sections.description: Comma-separated t values: one marker each.

sections.label: Labels:
sections.description: Each marker's label, formatted with t, the parameters and the definitions ({t:g} ns); empty for none.

sections.label: {filled_label}
sections.description: The curve with the parameter values written in (select to copy).

buttons.label: Fit
buttons.description: Fit this curve's free parameters to the displayed data (the 2-D distribution, or a marginal histogram)
